title: Iterating square mates equals conjugation for composite adjunctions
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be categories. Specify adjunctions $L_1:\mathcal A\rightleftarrows\mathcal B:R_1$, $L_2:\mathcal C\rightleftarrows\mathcal D:R_2$, $F_1:\mathcal A\rightleftarrows\mathcal C:U_1$ and $F_2:\mathcal B\rightleftarrows\mathcal D:U_2$, with the left adjoint written first. For an arbitrary natural transformation $\alpha:L_2F_1\to F_2L_1$, let $\beta:F_1R_1\to R_2F_2$ be its square mate under $L_1\dashv R_1$ and $L_2\dashv R_2$, and let $\gamma:R_1U_2\to U_1R_2$ be the square mate of $\beta$ under $F_2\dashv U_2$ and $F_1\dashv U_1$, with mates defined by unit insertion and counit contraction [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Then $\gamma$ equals the conjugate of $\alpha$ for the composite adjunctions $F_2L_1\dashv R_1U_2$ and $L_2F_1\dashv U_1R_2$ [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Conjugation here is the bijection between transformations of the two left adjoints and the reversed transformations of their right adjoints obtained by composing their natural Hom bijections. In particular this is an equality of the specified transformations, with their canonical functor associators and unitors.
